Please use English. You can use Google Translate if your English is not good.

Question Translation: Email delivery failures to the same addresses: "Undelivered Mail – Return to Sender"? What should I do to resolve this issue for all my replies to the email I received?

This is not a Thunderbird problem. What I means is, thunderbird is not creating the issue, so you can rest assured all is ok.

The server has sent you an email telling you that email could not be delivered. Usually the email offers a bit more information but these are the more common reasons for a return to sender.

1. Email address does not exist - it may be badly formatted or a typo error - suggest you check for typo errors. 2.Email address did exist but has now been deactivated, so it's correctly spelt but a dead account. 3. Email address does exist but the person has used up all their quota; mailbox is full, so server cannot accept any more mail until some space has been created. 4. Email rejected by server because it failed the server spam filter 5. Server has a temporary issue. 6. Email doesn’t comply with the authentication policies of the sending domain eg: rejected due to DMARC 5 Blocked - your email address or IP address has been put on a block list. Suggest you check this using this link: https://check.spamhaus.org/

content:
This is a recently discovered bug. The symptom is that if you previously attached a file, but the previous containing folder now no longer exists because it was deleted or renamed, when you later try to attach a file using the Write window's "Attach" button, it will silently fail. That is, clicking the button will appear to do nothing. The bug should be fixed in the next release.

In the meantime, a workaround is to drag-and-drop the file onto the Write window using the mouse.

Or, if you don't mind changing Thunderbird's Advanced Settings:

  • In <Settings | General | Config Editor> search for: "mail.compose.attach.dir".
  • The value (path) here must be changed to one that is still available (for example C:\).
  • Close and exit Thunderbird, then restart it (this step might not be necessary.)

Add a space then a dash then a capital P So Target says: "C:\Program Files\Mozilla Thunderbird\thunderbird.exe" -P click on 'Apply' and click 'OK'

This this get you access to Thunderbird so can remove the account ? After removing the account - also remove the stored passwords associated with that account. content:
Threading in Thunderbird and most other email clients depend on the messages' "Message-ID" and "References" headers to know to automatically associate them into threads. Threads can easily be broken by the sender, for example if they try to contribute to the thread but don't actually reply to a message within the thread. In that case, Thunderbird doesn't have any way to know they're part of the same conversation.

In your case, where you know there are disparate messages that are actually part of the same conversation, there's no real way to associate them. But I can think of a couple ways to get a similar effect...

- copy the relevant messages to a folder. That would mean you have duplicate messages, maybe not optimal.

- use the Tags feature to group messages into categories. Then use the Quick Filter to isolate them for viewing.

- If all the messages are in one folder, and you can build a query using the "Find Messages" feature (see <Edit | Find | Search Messages> or <Ctrl+Shift+F>) that finds them all, you could save this as a Virtual Search Folder>.

- I found this add-on, "Thunderbird Conversations" (https://addons.thunderbird.net/en-US/thunderbird/addon/gmail-conversation-view/). I don't actually quite understand what it does, but it's something you can investigate.

content: This is a stab in the dark, but when you open an attachment, Thunderbird actually saves a copy of the attachment in the operating system's temporary files location, then opens THAT. In Windows, the default temporary files folder is "C:\Users\(your account)\AppData\Local\Temp"; Thunderbird may create a sub-folder there for the attachment copy. But if, while Thunderbird is closed, you can locate that temporary file and delete it, maybe the symptom will go away.

Make sure you have a backup copy of the Profile in case something unexpected happens. And consider making regular backups of the Profile if your email collection is precious to you.
